commentary_segments.text: Another bipolar crystal oscillator is shown in this slide. It is again a single-pin oscillator. The positive feedback is easily recognizable. Indeed, a cross-coupled transistor pair presents a negative resistance of −2/g (see Chapter 2). This m resistance now compensates the series resistance of the crystal. The output is nicely buffered from the oscillation circuit itself, by means of a cascode. The biasing is fixed. The amplitude is limited by the Base-Emitter diodes of the cross-coupled transistor pair.
